stem: The shortest distance between the lines \(\bar{r}=\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)\) and \(\bar{r}=\left(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)+\mu\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)\) is

[Textbook defect: the printed alternatives are wrong. The shortest distance computes to \(\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx 0.98\), which matches none of the four printed values. The official key marks \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.87\), retained here to match the board.]

\(\bar{a_1}=(1,2,1),\ \bar{b_1}=(1,-1,-1),\ \bar{a_2}=(2,-1,-1),\ \bar{b_2}=(2,1,2)\).

\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=(-1,-4,3)\), so \(\left|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\right|=\sqrt{26}\).

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(1,-3,-2)\), and \(\left(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}\right)=(1)(-1)+(-3)(-4)+(-2)(3)=5\).

Shortest distance \(=\dfrac{|5|}{\sqrt{26}}=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}\approx 0.98\), whereas the printed values are \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\approx 0.58\), \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.71\), \(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 2.12\) and \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\approx 0.87\).

stem: Verify that point having position vector \(4\hat{i}-11\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) lies on the line \(\bar{r}=(6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\).
solution:
Replacing \(\bar{r}\) by \(4\hat{i}-11\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) we get,
\(4\hat{i}-11\hat{j}+2\hat{k}=(6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\)
\(\therefore 6+2\lambda=4,\ -4+7\lambda=-11,\ 5+3\lambda=2\)
From each of these equations we get the same value of \(\lambda\).
\(\therefore\) Given point lies on the given line.

Alternative Method: Equation \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\) can be written as \(\bar{r}-\bar{a}=\lambda\bar{b}\).
Thus point \(P(\bar{r})\) lies on the line if and only if \(\bar{r}-\bar{a}\) is a scalar multiple of \(\bar{b}\).
Equation of line is \(\bar{r}=(6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\).
\(\therefore \bar{a}=6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
The position vector of given point is \(\bar{r}=4\hat{i}-11\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{r}-\bar{a}=(4\hat{i}-11\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(6\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})=-2\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-3\hat{k}=-(2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=-1\bar{b}\), a scalar multiple of \(\bar{b}\).
\(\therefore\) Given point lies on the given line.

stem: Find the vector equation of the line passing through the point having position vector \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\) and perpendicular to vectors \(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
solution:
Let \(\bar{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
We know that \(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\) is perpendicular to both \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\).
\(\therefore \bar{b}\times\bar{c}\) is parallel to the required line.
\(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&1\\1&2&-1\end{vmatrix}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
Thus required line passes through \(\bar{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\) and parallel to \(-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore\) Its equation is \(\bar{r}=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k})+\lambda(-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

solution:
Let A, B, C be points with position vectors \(\bar{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) respectively.
\(\overline{BC}=\bar{c}-\bar{b}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k})=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
The required line passes through \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) and is parallel to \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
Its equation is \(\bar{r}=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\).

stem: Find the vector equation of the line passing through \(A(1,2,3)\) and \(B(2,3,4)\).
solution:
Let position vectors of points A and B be \(\bar{a}\) and \(\bar{b}\).
\(\therefore \bar{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore \bar{b}-\bar{a}=(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})-(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\)
The equation of the line passing through \(A(\bar{a})\) and \(B(\bar{b})\) is \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda(\bar{b}-\bar{a})\).
The equation of the required line is \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

stem: Find the Cartesian equations of the line passing through \(A(1,2,3)\) and having direction ratios \(2,3,7\).
solution:

Here \((x_1,y_1,z_1)=(1,2,3)\) and direction ratios are \(2,3,7\).

stem: Find the Cartesian equations of the line passing through the point \(A(2,1,-3)\) and perpendicular to vectors \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
solution:
We know that \(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\) is perpendicular to both \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\).
\(\therefore \bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&1\\1&2&-1\end{vmatrix}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) is parallel to the required line.
The direction ratios of the required line are \(-3,2,1\) and it passes through \(A(2,1,-3)\).
\(\therefore\) Its Cartesian equations are \(\frac{x-2}{-3}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z+3}{1}\).

subtopic: Vector and Cartesian Equations of a Line
stem: Find the angle between lines \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\).
solution:
Let \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\) be vectors along given lines.
\(\therefore \bar{b}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)
Angle between lines is same as the angle between \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\).
The angle between \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\) is given by,
\(\cos\theta=\frac{\bar{b}\cdot\bar{c}}{|\bar{b}|\cdot|\bar{c}|}=\frac{(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})}{3\times3}=\frac{0}{9}=0\)
\(\therefore \cos\theta=0\ \therefore \theta=90^\circ\)
Lines are perpendicular to each other.

stem: Show that lines \(\bar{r}=(-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+\lambda(-10\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(-10\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\) intersect each other. Find the position vector of their point of intersection.
solution:
The position vector of a variable point on the line \(\bar{r}=(-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+\lambda(-10\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) is \((-1-10\lambda)\hat{i}+(-3-\lambda)\hat{j}+(4+\lambda)\hat{k}\).
The position vector of a variable point on the line \(\bar{r}=(-10\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\) is \((-10-\mu)\hat{i}+(-1-3\mu)\hat{j}+(1+4\mu)\hat{k}\).
Given lines intersect each other if there exist some values of \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\) for which
\((-1-10\lambda)\hat{i}+(-3-\lambda)\hat{j}+(4+\lambda)\hat{k}=(-10-\mu)\hat{i}+(-1-3\mu)\hat{j}+(1+4\mu)\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore -1-10\lambda=-10-\mu,\ -3-\lambda=-1-3\mu\) and \(4+\lambda=1+4\mu\)
\(\therefore 10\lambda-\mu=9,\ \lambda-3\mu=-2\) and \(\lambda-4\mu=-3\quad\ldots(1)\)
Given lines intersect each other if this system is consistent
As \(\begin{vmatrix}10&-1&9\\1&-3&-2\\1&-4&-3\end{vmatrix}=10(9-8)+1(-3+2)+9(-4+3)=10-1-9=0\)
\(\therefore\) The system (1) is consistent and lines intersect each other.
Solving any two equations in system (1), we get \(\lambda=1,\ \mu=1\)
Substituting this value of \(\lambda\) in \((-1-10\lambda)\hat{i}+(-3-\lambda)\hat{j}+(4+\lambda)\hat{k}\) we get, \(-11\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore\) The position vector of their point of intersection is \(-11\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).

stem: Find the length of the perpendicular drawn from the point \(P(3,2,1)\) to the line \(\bar{r}=\left(7\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(-2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)\).
solution:
The length of the perpendicular is same as the distance of \(P\) from the given line. The distance of point \(P(\bar{\alpha})\) from the line \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\) is \(\sqrt{|\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a}|^2-\left[\dfrac{(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a})\cdot\bar{b}}{|\bar{b}|}\right]^2}\).

Here \(\bar{\alpha}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\bar{a}=7\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b}=-2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore \bar{\alpha}-\bar{a}=(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})-(7\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+6\hat{k})=-4\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\)

\(|\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a}|=\sqrt{(-4)^2+(-5)^2+(-5)^2}=\sqrt{16+25+25}=\sqrt{66}\)

\((\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a})\cdot\bar{b}=(-4\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-5\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=8-10-15=-17\)

\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(2)^2+(3)^2}=\sqrt{17}\)

The required length \(=\sqrt{|\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a}|^2-\left[\dfrac{(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{a})\cdot\bar{b}}{|\bar{b}|}\right]^2}=\sqrt{66-\left|\dfrac{-17}{\sqrt{17}}\right|^2}=\sqrt{66-17}=\sqrt{49}=7\) unit.

subtopic: Distance of a Point from a Line
stem: Find the distance of the point \(P(0,2,3)\) from the line \(\dfrac{x+3}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+4}{3}\).
solution:
Let \(M\) be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point \(P(0,2,3)\) to the given line. \(M\) lies on the line. Let co-ordinates of \(M\) be \((5\lambda-3,\,2\lambda+1,\,3\lambda-4)\).

The direction ratios of \(PM\) are \((5\lambda-3)-0,\,(2\lambda+1)-2,\,(3\lambda-4)-3\) i.e. \(5\lambda-3,\,2\lambda-1,\,3\lambda-7\).

The direction ratios of the given line are \(5,2,3\) and \(PM\) is perpendicular to the given line.

\(\therefore 5(5\lambda-3)+2(2\lambda-1)+3(3\lambda-7)=0\)

\(\therefore \lambda=1\)

\(\therefore\) The co-ordinates of \(M\) are \((2,3,-1)\).

The distance of \(P\) from the line is \(PM=\sqrt{(2-0)^2+(3-2)^2+(-1-3)^2}=\sqrt{21}\) unit.

subtopic: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
stem: Find the shortest distance between lines \(\bar{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-5\hat{k})\).
solution:
The shortest distance between lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda_1\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda_2\bar{b_2}\) is \(\left|\dfrac{(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})}{|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|}\right|\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}\), \(\bar{a_2}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_2}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}-\hat{j})=-\hat{i}+2\hat{k}\)

And \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&1&-3\\2&1&-5\end{vmatrix}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\)

\(\therefore |\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{4+16}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}\)

\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(-\hat{i}+2\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j})=2\)

The required shortest distance \(=\left|\dfrac{(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})}{|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|}\right|=\left|\dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{5}}\right|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\) unit.

subtopic: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
stem: Find the shortest distance between lines \(\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-3}{4}\) and \(\dfrac{x-2}{3}=\dfrac{y-4}{4}=\dfrac{z-5}{5}\).
solution:
The vector equations of given lines are \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+\mu(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})\).

The shortest distance between lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda\bar{b_2}\) is \(\left|\dfrac{(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})}{|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|}\right|\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\bar{a_2}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_2}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore \bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+5\hat{k})-(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)

And \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&3&4\\3&4&5\end{vmatrix}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)

\(|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|=\sqrt{1+4+1}=\sqrt{6}\)

\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=1\)

\(\therefore\) The required shortest distance \(=\left|\dfrac{(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})}{|\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}|}\right|=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\) unit.

subtopic: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
stem: Show that lines \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\) intersect each other.
solution:
Lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda_1\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda_2\bar{b_2}\) intersect each other if and only if \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\bar{a_2}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)

\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=\begin{vmatrix}3&-4&3\\2&-2&1\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix}=3(-2)+4(3)+3(-2)=-6+12-6=0\)

Given lines intersect each other.

subtopic: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
stem: Find the distance between parallel lines \(\bar{r}=(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\).
solution:
The distance between parallel lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda\bar{b}\) is given by \(d=\left|(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}\right|\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\bar{a_2}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore \bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=-\hat{i}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{b}=\dfrac{2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{3}\)

\(\therefore (\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\-1&0&1\\\frac{2}{3}&\frac{1}{3}&-\frac{2}{3}\end{vmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{3}\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\-1&0&1\\2&1&-2\end{vmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{3}\{-\hat{i}-\hat{k}\}\)

\(d=\left|(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}\right|=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\) unit.

Alternative Method: The distance between parallel lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda\bar{b}\) is same as the distance of point \(A(\bar{a_1})\) from the line \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda\bar{b}\), given by \(d=\sqrt{|\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}|^2-\left[\dfrac{(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot\bar{b}}{|\bar{b}|}\right]^2}\). Now \(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=-\hat{i}+\hat{k}\), \(|\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}|=\sqrt{2}\); \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot\bar{b}=(-\hat{i}+\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=-2+0-2=-4\), \(|\bar{b}|=3\). \(d=\sqrt{2-\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)^2}=\sqrt{2-\frac{16}{9}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\) unit.

subtopic: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
stem: Find the distance between parallel lines \(\dfrac{x}{2}=\dfrac{y}{-1}=\dfrac{z}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-1}{-1}=\dfrac{z-1}{2}\).
solution:
The vector equations of given lines are \(\bar{r}=\lambda(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\).

The distance between parallel lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda\bar{b}\) is given by \(d=\left|(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}\right|\).

Here \(\bar{a_1}=\bar{0}\), \(\bar{a_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore \bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{b}=\dfrac{2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}}{3}\)

\(\therefore (\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&1\\\frac{2}{3}&\frac{-1}{3}&\frac{2}{3}\end{vmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{3}\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&1\\2&-1&2\end{vmatrix}=\dfrac{1}{3}\{3\hat{i}-3\hat{k}\}=\hat{i}-\hat{k}\)

\(d=\left|(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\times\hat{b}\right|=\sqrt{2}\) unit.

stem: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the point having position vector \(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) and perpendicular to the vector \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
solution:

Here \(\bar{a}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k},\ \bar{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).

stem: Find the Cartesian equation of the plane passing through \(A(1, 2, 3)\) and the direction ratios of whose normal are \(3, 2, 5\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: The foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to a plane is \(M(2, 1, -2)\). Find the vector equation of the plane.
solution:
OM is normal to the plane.

\(\therefore\) The direction ratios of the normal are \(2, 1, -2\).

The plane passes through the point having position vector \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\) and vector \(\overline{OM}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\) is normal to it.

Its vector equation is \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\).

\(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=9\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the point \(A(-1, 2, -5)\) and parallel to vectors \(4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
solution:
The vector equation of the plane passing through point \(A(\bar{a})\) and parallel to \(\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\) is \(\bar{r}\cdot(\bar{b}\times\bar{c})=\bar{a}\cdot(\bar{b}\times\bar{c})\).

Here \(\bar{a}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-5\hat{k},\ \bar{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k},\ \bar{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ 4 & -1 & 3\\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}=-2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{a}\cdot(\bar{b}\times\bar{c})=(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-5\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k})=-9\).

The required equation is \(\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k})=-9\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the Cartesian equation of the plane \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}-\hat{j})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\).
solution:
Given plane is perpendicular to vector \(\bar{n}\), where

\(\bar{n}=\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{vmatrix}=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore\) The direction ratios of the normal are \(5, -2, -3\).

And plane passes through \(A(1, -1, 0)\).

\(\therefore\) Its Cartesian equation is \(a(x-x_1)+b(y-y_1)+c(z-z_1)=0\)

\(\therefore 5(x-1)-2(y+1)-3(z-0)=0\)

\(\therefore 5x-2y-3z-7=0\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through points \(A(1, 1, 2)\), \(B(0, 2, 3)\) and \(C(4, 5, 6)\).
solution:
Let \(\bar{a},\bar{b}\) and \(\bar{c}\) be position vectors of points \(A, B\) and \(C\) respectively.

\(\therefore \bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\ \bar{b}=2\hat{j}+3\hat{k},\ \bar{c}=4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore \bar{b}-\bar{a}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}-\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\).

\(\therefore (\bar{b}-\bar{a})\times(\bar{c}-\bar{a})=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ -1 & 1 & 1\\ 3 & 4 & 4\end{vmatrix}=7\hat{j}-7\hat{k}\).

The plane passes through \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) and \(7\hat{j}-7\hat{k}\) is normal to the plane.

\(\therefore\) Its equation is \((\bar{r}-\bar{a})\cdot(7\hat{j}-7\hat{k})=0\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot(7\hat{j}-7\hat{k})=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(7\hat{j}-7\hat{k})\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot(7\hat{j}-7\hat{k})=-7\) is the required equation.

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the vector equation of the plane which is at a distance of 6 unit from the origin and to which the vector \(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) is normal.
solution:
Here \(p=6\) and \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) \(\therefore |\bar{n}|=3\).

\(\therefore \hat{n}=\dfrac{\bar{n}}{|\bar{n}|}=\dfrac{2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}}{3}\).

The required equation is \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{n}=p\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\dfrac{2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}}{3}\right)=6\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=18\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the perpendicular distance of the origin from the plane \(x-3y+4z-6=0\).
solution:
First we write the given Cartesian equation in normal form, i.e. in the form \(lx+my+nz=p\).

Direction ratios of the normal are \(1, -3, 4\).

\(\therefore\) Direction cosines are \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}}, \dfrac{-3}{\sqrt{26}}, \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{26}}\).

Given equation can be written as \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}}x-\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{26}}y+\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{26}}z=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{26}}\).

\(\therefore\) The distance of the origin from the plane is \(\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{26}}\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the plane \(2x+y-2z=18\).
solution:
The direction ratios of the normal to the plane \(2x+y-2z=18\) are \(2, 1, -2\).

\(\therefore\) Direction cosines are \(\dfrac{2}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}, -\dfrac{2}{3}\).

The normal form of the given Cartesian equation is \(\dfrac{2}{3}x+\dfrac{1}{3}y-\dfrac{2}{3}z=6\).

\(\therefore p=6\).

The coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular are \((lp, mp, np)=\left(6\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right), 6\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right), 6\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)\right)\equiv(4, 2, -4)\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Reduce the equation \(\bar{r}\cdot(3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+12\hat{k})=8\) to the normal form and hence find (i) the length of the perpendicular from the origin to the plane (ii) direction cosines of the normal.
solution:
Here \(\bar{n}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+12\hat{k}\) \(\therefore |\bar{n}|=13\).

The required normal form is \(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{(3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+12\hat{k})}{13}=\dfrac{8}{13}\).

(ii) direction cosines of the normal are \(\dfrac{3}{13}, \dfrac{-4}{13}, \dfrac{12}{13}\).

subtopic: Equations of a Plane
stem: Find the vector equation of the plane passing through the point \((1, 0, 2)\) and the line of intersection of planes \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=8\) and \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})=3\).
solution:
The equation of the required plane is of the form \(\bar{r}\cdot(\bar{n_1}+\lambda\bar{n_2})-(d_1+\lambda d_2)=0\).

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left[(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\right]=8+3\lambda\) ... (1)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot((1+2\lambda)\hat{i}+(1+3\lambda)\hat{j}+(1+4\lambda)\hat{k})=8+3\lambda\).

The plane passes through the point \((1, 0, 2)\).

\(\therefore (\hat{i}+2\hat{k})\cdot((1+2\lambda)\hat{i}+(1+3\lambda)\hat{j}+(1+4\lambda)\hat{k})=8+3\lambda\)

\(\therefore (1+2\lambda)+2(1+4\lambda)=8+3\lambda\)

\(\therefore 1+2\lambda+2+8\lambda=8+3\lambda\)

\(\therefore 7\lambda=5\)

\(\therefore \lambda=\dfrac{5}{7}\) ... (2)

From (1) and (2) we get

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left((\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\dfrac{5}{7}(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\right)=8+3\left(\dfrac{5}{7}\right)\)

\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot(17\hat{i}+22\hat{j}+27\hat{k})=71\).

subtopic: Angle Between Planes and Line-Plane Angle
stem: Find the angle between planes \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=8\) and \(\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=3\).
solution:
Normal to the given planes are \(\bar{n_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{n_2}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
The acute angle \(\theta\) between normals is given by \(\cos\theta=\left|\dfrac{\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}}{|\bar{n_1}|\cdot|\bar{n_2}|}\right|\).
\(\therefore\cos\theta=\left|\dfrac{(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{\sqrt{6}\cdot\sqrt{6}}\right|=\left|\dfrac{-3}{6}\right|=\dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(\therefore\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}\qquad\therefore\theta=60^\circ=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\).
The acute angle between normals \(\bar{n_1}\) and \(\bar{n_2}\) is \(60^\circ\).
\(\therefore\) The angle between the given planes is \(60^\circ\).

subtopic: Angle Between Planes and Line-Plane Angle
stem: Find the angle between the line \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) and the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=8\).
solution:
The angle between the line \(\bar{r}=\bar{a}+\lambda\bar{b}\) and the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=d\) is given by \(\sin\theta=\left|\dfrac{\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}}{|\bar{b}|\cdot|\bar{n}|}\right|\).
Here \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=2-1+1=2\).
\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{1+1+1}=\sqrt{3}\) and \(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{4+1+1}=\sqrt{6}\).
\(\therefore\sin\theta=\left|\dfrac{\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}}{|\bar{b}|\cdot|\bar{n}|}\right|=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\).
\(\therefore\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)\).

subtopic: Coplanarity of Two Lines
stem: Show that lines \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) and \(\bar{r}=(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\) are coplanar. Find the equation of the plane determined by them.
solution:
Lines \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda_1\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\lambda_2\bar{b_2}\) are coplanar if and only if \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0\).
Here \(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\bar{a_2}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_1}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=\begin{vmatrix}3 & -4 & 3\\ 2 & -2 & 1\\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{vmatrix}=3(-2)+4(3)+3(-2)=-6+12-6=0\).
\(\therefore\) Given lines are coplanar.
Now \(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k}\\ 2 & -2 & 1\\ 1 & -2 & 2\end{vmatrix}=-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
The equation of the plane determined by them is \((\bar{r}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0\).
\(\therefore\bar{r}\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=\bar{a_1}\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})\).
\(\therefore\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k})\).
\(\therefore\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=-3\).
\(\therefore\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=3\).

subtopic: Distance of a Point from a Plane
stem: Find the distance of the point \(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) from the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=6\).
solution:
Here \(\bar{a}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\bar{n}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
\(\therefore|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(1)^2+(-2)^2}=3\).
\(\therefore\hat{n}=\dfrac{-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{3}\).
The normal form of the equation of the given plane is \(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{3}=2\), \(\therefore p=2\).
Now, \(\bar{a}\cdot\hat{n}=(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot\dfrac{-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{3}=\dfrac{(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})}{3}=\dfrac{-15}{3}=-5\).
\(\therefore\bar{a}\cdot\hat{n}=-5\).
The required distance is given by \(|p-\bar{a}\cdot\hat{n}|=|2-(-5)|=|7|=7\).
Therefore the distance of the point \(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) from the plane \((-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=6\) is 7 unit.
